hypothesis: A generic profit floor and trailing stop activated before HYPE's eight-hour soft boundary may retain more after-cost profit than the active no-target contract.
decision: Reaffirm rejection of the frozen 25/15/10, 40/15/20, and 60/15/30 bps activation/floor/trail policies. The eighth resolved HYPE lifecycle is a loss that the two tighter policies would have converted to a small estimated gain, but selecting that row alone reverses the all-live conclusion. Across all eight HYPE lifecycles, every policy reduced mean normalized after-cost return by more than 81 bps per trade. Preserve the active exit contract and do not apply these universal tight locks to the open lifecycle or a future profile.
falsifier: A prospectively frozen pre-soft profit-protection policy that improves actual after-cost exits across multiple non-adjacent profile-matched live windows without reducing mean normalized return or increasing loss concentration would update this rejection; changed source-prefix hashes would invalidate the present audit.
limitations: Eight resolved HYPE closes remain sparse and are not independent market samples.
The all-live mechanism sample spans four source profiles and seven process runs with differing sizing contracts.
Basis-point normalization removes notional scale but does not construct a counterfactual shared-portfolio equity path.
Completed one-minute bars cannot reconstruct intraminute trigger ordering.
Counterfactual fills reuse each actual exit fill/reference ratio and fee rate rather than submitted orders.
The current aligned v11 HYPE short remains open and is excluded from resolved policy comparisons.
